findings.summary: The new rule `starts = !suppress && !current?.headingForm` hides more than nested checklists. A bold item like `**OQ-2 ...**` or a numbered question placed after a resolved `### OQ-1` heading becomes part of OQ-1's text and is not counted even if open. Not exploitable (maintainer-authored RFCs); matches task scope; the per-file count test catches changes in today's RFCs. Suggestion: start a new block when a line matches OQ-n or Qn explicitly.
